column1: # Boundary cases for the LINEAGE axis of the faceted models ontology.
# Every row is a case R1-R7 do not decide cleanly. Both the reading CHOSEN
# and the reading REJECTED are recorded, so overruling any row is a one-line
# change rather than a re-derivation. The three run-A-vs-run-B disputes the
# owner named are at L-01 (embedding/factorization), L-04 (Hopfield) and
# L-09 (slot attention); their full argument is in MERGE_RATIONALE.md section 2.

column3: rule_in_tension
column4: reading_chosen
column5: reading_rejected
column6: why
column7: consequence_if_wrong

column2: The two umbrella roots: `Embedding model` (A) vs `Factorization model` (B)
column3: R6 vs the faceted design
column4: BOTH deleted. Their shared content -- `the learned object is a learned low-rank table` -- is connectivity=factorized. What survives is three design families: `Matrix factorization` (root), `Knowledge-graph embedding model` (root) and `word2vec` (under MLP).
column5: Keeping one of the two as a root, with the other run's members folded in
column6: Both agents independently named their own version as their weakest set, which is what an axis value wearing lineage clothing looks like from the inside. Run A's division (word / node / KG) is by data structure consumed, a rejected characteristic; run B's six children are, in its own words, `a list` rather than values of one variable.
column7: A `proportion of papers using an embedding/factorization model` cut is no longer answerable from lineage alone -- it is answerable as connectivity=factorized, which is a different (and larger) set. If the owner wants the lineage cut back, one root re-appears and the three families become its children.

column2: `Variational autoencoder`'s parent after the `Autoencoder` root is deleted
column3: R1 vs R6
column4: Child of `Directed graphical model`, pinning topology=encoder-decoder and attributes=stochastic-latent
column5: (a) VAE as a root of its own; (b) VAE kept under a surviving `Autoencoder` root
column6: Run A pre-committed to this repair in its own SELF_AUDIT 2.6, and it is R1-grounded: Kingma & Welling open by framing the work as inference and learning in `directed probabilistic models with continuous latent variables`. R6 then forbids the root reading, because the directed latent-variable model IS in this tree.
column7: If wrong, VAE and its four descendants become a 5-node root and the `Directed graphical model` sibling set loses its only deep-learning member. Cheap to reverse: one edge.

column3: R1 (which does not apply to pre-paper-culture statistics) -- A/B10
column4: Child of `Matrix factorization` (run B)
column5: Child of `Linear model` (run A)
column6: PCA is truncated SVD: the learned object is a pair of low-rank factors, which is the parent's characteristic exactly. It also keeps `Linear model` to supervised affine predictors, repairing the mixed-kind set run A flagged as its 3rd-worst.
column7: Low. CCA went the other way (to `Linear model`) on the same kind of judgement, so the two sit in different roots although a reader may expect them together. Zero corpus support for `pca` as a name, so no count moves.

column2: Hopfield networks and the `Energy-based network` root
column3: the admission rule / the backbone test vs R6
column4: No energy-based root. `Hopfield network` and `Boltzmann machine` under `Undirected graphical model` (run A); `Neural energy-based model` is algorithm-side
column5: Run B's `Energy-based network` root with three division children
column6: A deep EBM is an unchanged network plus a new objective and a sampling procedure, which the backbone test sends to algorithms. Admitting the root would re-import an objective as a lineage root, which is exactly what deleting `Autoencoder` and `GAN` removes. Hopfield's 1982 Ising framing is literally an undirected graphical model.
column7: ~5 corpus names containing `energy-based` produce an algorithm mention plus a backbone rather than a lineage node. Mechanical to reverse: re-root two nodes.

column3: R1 vs R2 (A/B21)
column4: Direct child of `Feedforward network`, sibling of `Deep Sets`
column5: Child of `Deep Sets` (run A)
column6: The two are contemporaneous (both 2017) and the shared per-element-MLP-plus-symmetric-pool construction is a similarity, which R2 names as never an edge. The shared construction is now visible as connectivity=set-aggregation, so nothing is lost by refusing the edge.
column7: Low. `proportion using a permutation-invariant set network` is answered on the connectivity axis either way.

column2: `Conditional GAN` after the `GAN` root is deleted
column3: R1; the owner's disposition on GAN
column4: Deleted. pix2pix -> `U-Net` (its generator), CycleGAN -> pix2pix, BigGAN -> `DCGAN`, SRGAN -> `ResNet`
column5: Keeping `Conditional GAN` as a lineage node under one of the wiring families
column6: With adversarial training on the algorithm side, what `Conditional GAN` asserts is `the networks take an extra input`, which is a conditioning scheme, not a design lineage. Each named member has a real wiring parent that the paper states.
column7: BigGAN's parent is the weakest edge in this group: it is a large class-conditional convolutional generator, and `DCGAN` is an ancestry claim rather than a framing claim.

column3: the admission rule; R4(2) -- A/B31
column4: A node under `Boosted tree ensemble` (run A)
column5: Not a node at all: AdaBoost is the reweighting procedure (run B)
column6: The resulting weighted ensemble is a separable, runnable learned object, and its canonical base learner is a stump, so it has a tree parent. Dropping it would leave `Boosted tree ensemble` with one child and make it a rename of GBDT.
column7: AdaBoost over non-tree base learners has no home. If the node is refused, the boosted/bagged division collapses to a single GBDT chain.

column3: R1 vs the contribution being a scaling rule
column4: Child of `MobileNet` (run A)
column5: Child of run B's deleted `Depthwise-separable network` grouping
column6: The grouping node was an axis value (connectivity=depthwise-separable) and is deleted, so run B's parent no longer exists. The MBConv block inheritance from MobileNetV2 is the only remaining lineage claim.
column7: Run B's objection stands: the introducing framing is about compound scaling, which is arguably a procedure. If so, EfficientNet moves up to `CNN`.

column3: R1 vs R2
column4: A root (run A), pinning connectivity=cross-attention and attributes=permutation-equivariance, with `SlotFormer` as a child
column5: A descent child of `Transformer` (run B)
column6: The paper defines its mechanism against dot-product attention (citing Luong), by swapping the softmax axis so slots compete, plus a recurrent update. `Both use attention` is a shared primitive, which R2 names explicitly as never an edge.
column7: An object-centric cluster of ~8 corpus names counts as Transformer work at the depth-1 cut. Run B itself called this its least settled placement.

column3: R7 (a flat family stays flat) vs the owner's instruction
column4: Flat: BERT, ViT, GPT, LLaMA, T5, ... all attach directly, each pinning its own topology
column5: Re-introducing any grouping level under `Transformer`
column6: The owner fixes this: encoder-only / decoder-only / encoder-decoder is topology, not lineage, and the cut survives on the topology axis. There is no root-count or width bound, and width is a finding.
column7: R7 means this set stays flat until a design pass opens it. If the width is a defect rather than a finding, the repair is NOT the deleted division -- it would have to be a principle that is a property of the model and is not already an axis. SELF_AUDIT 3 says what little is on offer.

column2: `Normalizing flow` kept as a root although invertibility is an attribute
column3: R6; the owner's instruction to judge
column4: Root kept, with coupling / autoregressive / continuous-time as lineage substructure
column5: Deleting it and scattering NICE, RealNVP, Glow, MAF, IAF, FFJORD across their backbones
column6: NICE -> RealNVP -> Glow is a real R1 descent spine with the paper framings to match, which is what distinguishes a named design family from an axis value. MODELS_AXES.md itself refers to `a Normalizing flow family`.
column7: If deleted, six nodes lose any parent at all -- a coupling layer has no backbone family to fall back to -- so this is the clearest case in the file where deleting an axis-shaped root would destroy content.

column2: `Group-equivariant CNN` kept although equivariance is an attribute
column3: the owner's keep/delete rule
column4: Kept as a named design family under `CNN`, pinning attributes=euclidean-equivariance, with `Steerable CNN` as a child
column5: Deleting it as an axis composition (CNN + equivariance), the way run B's `Equivariant graph network` was deleted
column6: G-CNN is a founding paper with a named descendant; `Equivariant graph network` was a grouping node invented to hold SchNet/EGNN/DimeNet, which each have their own framing. The test is whether the node names a design or names the property.
column7: Low. If deleted, Steerable CNN attaches to `CNN` and the equivariance cut is unaffected (it lives on the attributes axis).

column2: `Continuous normalizing flow`: division value or descent node
column3: R4(2) -- one child is a rename
column4: A `descent` node with parents {`Normalizing flow`, `Neural ODE`} and one child, FFJORD
column5: A third `division` child of `Normalizing flow` beside coupling and autoregressive (run B's shape)
column6: As a division node it would have exactly one child, which R4(2) forbids. As a descent node it is a named design (Chen et al.) whose single descendant is a genuine separate release, which R4 does not forbid. The cost is that the three-way split is no longer a clean division.
column7: The flow division is not total over its parent's extension. Declared rather than fudged; a design pass adding a second continuous-time member repairs it.

column3: R1, R5
column4: Parents {`Matrix factorization`, `word2vec`}, R5 hybrid
column5: `Matrix factorization` alone, or a `Word embedding model` grouping parent (both runs)
column6: The paper's own abstract names both lineages: it `combines the advantages of the two major model families: global matrix factorization and local context window methods`. This is an R1 framing claim, not a reconstruction.
column7: Zero corpus support for `glove`, so nothing counts either way today.

column3: R1 (paper framing) vs the learned object -- run B's B-12
column4: Child of `Feedforward network (MLP)`, pinning connectivity=factorized
column5: Under an embedding/factorization umbrella (both runs), or as a root of its own
column6: Mikolov frames the two architectures as the feedforward NNLM with the nonlinear hidden layer removed, so R1 is satisfiable here and was not satisfiable under either umbrella (run B declared its own placement an R1 violation). Run B's objection -- `it would sit beside MLP classifiers it shares nothing with` -- is answered by the pin: what it shares with GloVe and TransE is connectivity=factorized.
column7: Low in this corpus: word2vec, GloVe, fastText, node2vec and DeepWalk have ZERO corpus support and are kept purely because the ontology covers the field.

column2: `Liquid state machine` as the sole survivor of the spiking root
column3: R6; the owner's disposition on SNN
column4: Kept under `Reservoir network`, pinning attributes=spiking. Integrate-and-fire and conductance-based networks are deleted
column5: Keeping a `Spiking neural network` lineage node with the two neuron-model children (run B)
column6: A neuron model is what the substrate attribute's values ARE, so dividing lineage by it duplicates the axis. A spiking reservoir, by contrast, is a design: a fixed random spiking recurrent pool with a trained readout.
column7: Zero corpus support for anything spiking, so this costs no counts. If no spiking design lineage is wanted at all, delete one node.

column3: the faceted design (every lineage node pins the other axes)
column4: Left unpinned and reported as axis gaps: `Rule-based model`, `Probabilistic graphical model`, `Recursive neural network`, `Neural operator`, `3D Gaussian splatting`
column5: Forcing an approximate value, or deleting the nodes
column6: An empty pin means `same as parent`; at a root it means the axis has no value. Forcing `tree-traversal` onto a rule set or `convolution` onto a neural operator would make the connectivity axis look complete when it is not.
column7: If the connectivity axis grows values later, five nodes need revisiting. `3D Gaussian splatting` is correctly unpinnable -- it has no learned units wired to one another.

column3: the admission rule; the SimCLR fixed point -- B/B-10
column4: A node under `ViT`, pinning topology=encoder-decoder
column5: Algorithm-only: masked reconstruction is an objective and the model is the ViT backbone
column6: The asymmetric encoder/lightweight-decoder pair is an architectural choice the paper makes and releases, not only a loss. Run A pre-committed to exactly this placement if the autoencoder root fell.
column7: Moderate: if MAE is algorithm-only then so are several SSL families, and the same question returns for DINOv2.

column2: Ridge, lasso and elastic net as nodes
column3: R3 (`every separately named release is a node`) vs the admission rule
column4: Not nodes: recorded in `notes` on `Linear regression` (run A)
column5: Three nodes under `Linear regression` plus a two-parent `Elastic net` (run B)
column6: They are not separately named *releases*; they are the same learned object (a weight vector) fitted under different penalties, and the penalty is part of the fitting procedure, which the brief puts on the algorithm side.
column7: Low. `ridge regression` and `lasso` mentions resolve to `Linear regression` rather than to their own nodes.

column3: A/B09 vs the faceted design
column4: Deleted: it is attributes=bayesian-weights on whatever lineage node the paper names
column5: A node under `Feedforward network` (both runs)
column6: Both runs flagged it: run A called the MLP edge `the one I would drop first`, run B listed it as a cross-cutting property placed by compromise. A Bayesian U-Net and a Bayesian GNN are the same property on different lineages, which is the definition of an axis value.
column7: `bayesian neural network` mentions produce an attribute plus (often) no named lineage, so they fall out of family shares. Reported as a finding.

column3: R1 vs R5 composite -- B/B-06
column4: Detectors are nodes in their own lineage; the backbone is recorded per run, not as a parent edge
column5: A parent edge from each detector to every backbone it is paired with
column6: `Faster R-CNN with a ResNet-50 backbone` is a configuration, not a named release; the edge would make the DAG dense and double-count every backbone.
column7: Low for the tree, high for compute estimation: the backbone carries most of the FLOPs, so the run record must hold the pairing.

column2: NICE -> RealNVP -> Glow flattened under `Coupling-layer flow`
column3: R1 (a real chain) vs R4(2)
column4: All three flat under `Coupling-layer flow`, predecessors in `notes` (run B)
column5: The R1 chain NICE -> RealNVP -> Glow (run A)
column6: The chain would leave `Coupling-layer flow` with exactly one child, making it a rename of NICE and failing R4(2). Flattening a derivation series with the predecessor in notes is the precedent both runs already use for GPT generations.
column7: `what descends from NICE` cannot be answered from edges. Same trade-off run A declared at its B02.

column3: the brief's section 4.7 worked table
column4: Directly under `Transformer`, exactly as the brief's row writes it
column5: One level deeper, under an encoder-only node (BOTH runs)
column6: Both runs deviated from the brief to keep their encoder/decoder division total. The division is deleted, so the deviation is gone and the brief's literal reading is restored for free.
column7: None -- this is the one disagreement the refactor settles without a judgement call.

column3: R3 (spelling vs node) -- A/B23, B/B-16
column4: `ChatGPT`, `Codex`, `Claude`, `Gemini`, `GPT-4` are nodes under the family their vendor documentation supports
column5: Quarantining them until an architecture is published, or treating ChatGPT as a spelling of a GPT release
column6: The served model behind a product changes over time, so it is not `the same release under a different string`. These are among the most-named artifacts in the corpus (GPT-4 at 33 papers, ChatGPT at 16) and dropping them would gut the dimension.
column7: A wrong parent misattributes a share at a topology cut; the artifact-level count stays right. Midjourney has no vendor statement and is deliberately left for a design pass rather than guessed.

column2: `Knowledge-graph embedding model` as a grouping root
column3: R4(3) vs the rejected characteristic `data structure consumed`
column4: Kept as a root with four members, characteristic stated as a SCORING design
column5: Dissolving it into two roots (`TransE` and `DistMult`), or filing it under `Matrix factorization` via RESCAL
column6: `A triple scored by an algebraic form on three looked-up vectors` is a design, not a data structure -- but it is the closest this file comes to the rejected characteristic, so it is declared here and ranked first in SELF_AUDIT 2.
column7: If dissolved, two more roots appear and the KG-embedding cut is lost; if filed under matrix factorization, TransE's explicit contrast with tensor-factorization models is read as descent, which reading (d) forbids.
